title: LOVB Los Angeles names L.A. Clippers’ Intuit Dome as home venue
content:
Alexis Ohanian’s latest sports venture, LOVB Los Angeles, will play its inaugural season at Intuit Dome in Inglewood, Calif., the company announced Wednesday. The $2 billion arena, which opened in 2024 as the home of the NBA’s Los Angeles Clippers, will be one of the highest-profile homes in professional women’s sports.

The move puts professional women’s volleyball inside one of the newest major-league arenas in the country as the franchise attempts to establish itself in Los Angeles’ crowded sports market.

“Intuit Dome is the best new arena in sports, full stop,” Ohanian told The Athletic. “If we’re serious about building women’s volleyball into a major professional sport in LA, our athletes and fans deserve an iconic home. This is exactly the kind of stage we want for LOVB LA.

“It raises the ceiling for the entire business. You’re giving sponsors a premium platform, giving fans a destination they’re excited to come to, and giving our athletes an environment that reflects the caliber of the product. It sends a very clear signal about our ambition for this franchise and for women’s sports in LA.”

Ohanian, founder of Seven Seven Six investment firm, was a founding investor in NWSL club Angel City FC and later became the controlling owner of Athlos, the women’s track competition. His investment in LOVB extends that portfolio into volleyball at a time when women’s professional volleyball is growing exponentially.

“The fundamentals are impossible to ignore,” Ohanian said as a response to why he invested in volleyball in the first place. “Volleyball has a massive participation base, an enormous young and female audience, and some of the best athletes in the world, but the professional opportunity in the U.S. hasn’t matched that demand. I’ve seen what happens when you properly invest in women’s sports. The fans were already here. The talent was already here. The opportunity is to build the product and platform they deserve. I remember how excited I was to launch Angel City FC because of all the energy around women’s soccer in 2019 and women’s volleyball right now feels 100x more inevitable.”

LOVB launched its professional competition in 2024 with six teams in Austin, Atlanta, Houston, Madison, Omaha and Salt Lake City. The professional league sits atop a larger volleyball organization that stretches from youth clubs and grassroots programs to the professional level. LOVB LA is its seventh franchise. Earlier this year, LOVB hired sports investment bank Inner Circle Sports, which previously advised the NWSL on its expansion process, to advise on its next phase of expansion and long-term growth.

The Los Angeles franchise has already signaled that it intends to operate at the top end of that ecosystem. It recently announced a high-profile roster and hired Brazilian coaching legend José “Zé Roberto” Guimarães, one of volleyball’s most decorated coaches. Guimarães has won three Olympic gold medals as a head coach: one with Brazil’s men and two with its women.

Southern California has one of the country’s deepest volleyball cultures, producing elite indoor and beach players and supporting major collegiate programs. Los Angeles will become an even bigger focal point for the sport over the next two years as the city prepares to host the 2028 Olympics. Intuit Dome will host the official 5×5 basketball tournaments during the LA28 Olympic Games.

Emerging professional leagues have historically faced a difficult arena equation: Smaller buildings are easier to fill and less expensive to operate, but they can also limit ticket inventory, premium hospitality, sponsorship opportunities and the perception of the product. Intuit Dome gives LOVB LA the opposite proposition. Rather than starting small and trying to graduate into a major arena, the franchise is beginning in a building designed for one of the NBA’s most valuable markets.

LOVB LA will begin introducing itself to that market before its inaugural season begins in January 2027. The franchise will formally unveil its team brand, logo, colors and visual identity during an event at Intuit Dome on Sept. 25.

“We’ve worked closely with the Intuit Dome team to build LOVB LA into the venue calendar alongside the Clippers and other events,” Ohanian said. “This is about much more than putting a volleyball court on the floor. We want LOVB LA to feel at home there, with real opportunities for branding, merchandise and creating a distinct experience for our fans and welcome Clippers fans to join us on this journey.”
